cands.bio: Sacramento City Council member for District 8 since 2020, the first Hmong American elected to it. Earlier served on the Sacramento City Unified school board (2016-2020). Lecturer in ethnic studies at Sacramento State and co-founder of Hmong Innovating Politics. Daughter of Hmong refugees.

controversies.text: In late May 2026, videos resurfaced showing Vang, a Sacramento City Council member, not saying the Pledge of Allegiance at multiple council meetings. The clips drew backlash from critics. Fox News reported it had asked her for comment. Her own explanation is not included here.

endorsements.text: State Sen. Angelique Ashby (D), Working Families Party, Justice Democrats PAC, Sacramento Democratic Socialists of America, and Our Revolution.
California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, National Nurses United, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Sunrise Movement, and The Sacramento Bee.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm her exact birth year; Wikipedia gives 1984 or 1985. We found nothing on her position on homestead property taxes. We found no record of Sacramento City Council or school board actions on data centers, rezonings, farmland or growth limits. We found no documented stance on H-1B visas, suppressors or red-flag laws, or on teacher pay, homeschooling or abortion clinics. The campaign site's About page and the end of the Ballotpedia page were cut off, so anything past those points was not read.

qual.background: Elected to the Sacramento City Unified school board in 2016 and to the Sacramento City Council in 2020, re-elected unopposed in 2024. Co-founded the community organization Hmong Innovating Politics in 2013 and has lectured at Sacramento State since 2015.
qual.why: She has held local elected office for about ten years, including council budget and policy work, but has no state or federal legislative, legal or executive-branch experience.
qual.label: She has held local elected office for about ten years, including council budget and policy work, but has no state or federal legislative, legal or executive-branch experience.

stop-data-centers.evidence: She says she signed Sen. Bernie Sanders' moratorium on new data center construction and would fight to end tax giveaways for data center developers and make them cover the rate increases their energy use causes.

land-for-floridians.evidence: She says she will fight for federal laws that prevent big corporations from buying up single-family homes.

workers-first.evidence: She says ICE cannot be reformed and calls for abolishing it, defunding it, and creating a pathway to citizenship. She also says she fought to make Sacramento a sanctuary city and is working to ban ICE from city property.

clean-money.evidence: She says she takes no corporate PAC money and no AIPAC money, and wants to ban dark-money super PACs and congressional stock trading.

second-amendment.evidence: She says she opposes Flock Safety license-plate cameras and the expansion of AI surveillance networks, and that she led the fight against Flock cameras on the City Council.

pro-life.evidence: She says she supports federal protections guaranteeing the right to choose and requiring insurers to cover full reproductive care.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: She says she will resist efforts to divert public dollars to charter schools or private voucher programs.

back-police-order.evidence: In 2023 she voted on the Sacramento City Council to shift $6 million away from police overtime and unfilled vacancies into expanded hours for the homeless behavioral health department; the council majority rejected the proposal.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 8 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 4 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia says she was born in Sacramento and grew up in the Meadowview and Oak Park neighborhoods, and her campaign site says she was born and raised in Sacramento.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says she is the only candidate to have signed Sen. Bernie Sanders' moratorium on new data center construction. Says she will protect communities from massive data centers and end tax giveaways to developers.
Says she will fight to massively increase federal funding for new construction and make it easier to build more housing for teachers, nurses and working families.

cands.bio: Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 7th District (Sacramento area), first elected in a 2005 special election. Earlier a deputy assistant to the president in the Clinton administration and a government affairs consultant and lobbyist. Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by U.S. Sens. Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff, Rep. Nancy Pelosi, the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Teachers Association and Equality California.
Gov. Gavin Newsom endorsed her re-election ahead of the June 2026 primary, according to her campaign site.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Matsui on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and charters. We found no deeds on development or growth limits, and no news-documented controversies or foreign-government ties in the sources reviewed. Her statements on immigration enforcement, abortion and conservation come from her own campaign site, and her gun-policy position comes from Wikipedia. We did not review the underlying records for these. Her birth year of 1944 comes from Wikipedia only.

votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
